title: Conjecture 1.3 (Dreier and Toruńczyk)
context_text: Bounded twin-width classes were shown to be $\chi$-bounded in [BGK+21] and subsequently shown to be polynomially $\chi$-bounded in [PS23, BT25]. Dreier and Toruńczyk asked whether polynomial $\chi$-boundedness also holds for bounded merge-width. The present paper proves $\chi$-boundedness (Theorem 1.2) but leaves the polynomial strengthening open.
paper_contribution: Proves $\chi$-boundedness of bounded merge-width classes (Theorem 1.2), a strictly weaker result than polynomial $\chi$-boundedness; the conjecture itself remains open.
paper_title: $χ$-Boundedness and Neighbourhood Complexity of Bounded Merge-Width Graphs

title: Question 1.4
statement_text: Is the class $\{G:\operatorname{mw}_{1}(G)\leqslant k\}$, with $k$ arbitrary, $\chi$-bounded?
context_text: Merge-width (Dreier and Toruńczyk) is defined through merge sequences: for a graph $G$, a merge sequence is $(\mathcal{P}_1,R_1),\dots,(\mathcal{P}_m,R_m)$ where each $\mathcal{P}_i$ is a partition of $V(G)$, $\mathcal{P}_1$ is the partition into singletons, $\mathcal{P}_m=\{V(G)\}$, each $\mathcal{P}_i$ is coarser than or equal to $\mathcal{P}_{i-1}$; $R_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq R_m\subseteq\binom{V(G)}{2}$ are sets of resolved pairs; and for any two (possibly equal) parts $A,B\in\mathcal{P}_i$, the unresolved pairs between $A$ and $B$ (those not in $R_i$) are either all edges or all non-edges of $G$. Its radius-$r$ width is the maximum, over all steps $i\ge2$ and vertices $v$, of the number of parts of $\mathcal{P}_{i-1}$ reachable from $v$ by a path of length at most $r$ in the graph $(V(G),R_i)$ of resolved pairs. The radius-$r$ merge-width $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)$ is the minimum radius-$r$ width of a merge sequence for $G$, and a class has bounded merge-width if there is $f$ with $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)\le f(r)$ for all $G$ in the class and all $r$. Bounded merge-width generalises bounded expansion and bounded twin-width, and is stable under first-order transductions. A class is $\chi$-bounded if the chromatic number of its graphs is bounded by a function of their clique number $\omega$. The authors prove that every graph with $\operatorname{mw}_2(G)\le k$ and $\omega(G)\le t$ has $\chi(G)\le(t+1)!\,k^{2t-2}$, so bounded merge-width classes are $\chi$-bounded; radius $2$ is used in a single lemma (a colouring lemma for structurally $\omega$-bounded merge sequences), the rest of the proof needs only radius $1$, and it is unclear whether radius $2$ is necessary. A negative answer would require a class of bounded radius-1 merge-width and bounded clique number (possibly triangle-free) with unbounded chromatic number; such a class must contain arbitrarily large bicliques, since graphs of bounded radius-1 merge-width without $K_{t,t}$ subgraph are degenerate, and must have bounded symmetric difference (every induced subgraph has two vertices whose neighbourhoods differ on a bounded set). Shift graphs, a classical example of triangle-free graphs with large chromatic number, do not have bounded radius-1 merge-width.

title: Conjecture 1.7
statement_text: A class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded merge-width if and only if every first-order transduction of $\mathcal{C}$ has linear neighbourhood complexity.
context_text: Merge-width (Dreier and Toruńczyk) is defined through merge sequences: for a graph $G$, a merge sequence is $(\mathcal{P}_1,R_1),\dots,(\mathcal{P}_m,R_m)$ where each $\mathcal{P}_i$ is a partition of $V(G)$, $\mathcal{P}_1$ is the partition into singletons, $\mathcal{P}_m=\{V(G)\}$, each $\mathcal{P}_i$ is coarser than or equal to $\mathcal{P}_{i-1}$; $R_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq R_m\subseteq\binom{V(G)}{2}$ are sets of resolved pairs; and for any two (possibly equal) parts $A,B\in\mathcal{P}_i$, the unresolved pairs between $A$ and $B$ (those not in $R_i$) are either all edges or all non-edges of $G$. Its radius-$r$ width is the maximum, over all steps $i\ge2$ and vertices $v$, of the number of parts of $\mathcal{P}_{i-1}$ reachable from $v$ by a path of length at most $r$ in the graph $(V(G),R_i)$ of resolved pairs. The radius-$r$ merge-width $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)$ is the minimum radius-$r$ width of a merge sequence for $G$, and a class has bounded merge-width if there is $f$ with $\operatorname{mw}_r(G)\le f(r)$ for all $G$ in the class and all $r$. Bounded merge-width generalises bounded expansion and bounded twin-width, and is stable under first-order transductions. The neighbourhood complexity of $G$ is $\pi_G(p)=\max_{X\subseteq V(G),|X|=p}\#\{N(v)\cap X : v\notin X\}$, extended to classes by taking the maximum over the class; it is linear if $\pi(p)=O(p)$. A first-order transduction maps a graph to the graphs obtained by colouring its vertices with a bounded number of unary predicates, defining new edges by a fixed first-order formula, and taking an induced subgraph. The authors prove that every graph with $\operatorname{mw}_2(G)\le k$ has $\pi_G(p)\le k2^{k+2}p$ (radius $2$ is optimal since $k$-degenerate graphs have bounded radius-1 merge-width but neighbourhood complexity $\Theta(p^k)$); since bounded merge-width is preserved by transductions, this gives the left-to-right implication. Reidl, Villaamil and Stavropoulos showed that linear neighbourhood complexity of balls of every radius characterises bounded expansion among subgraph-closed classes, but balls are meaningless for dense graphs of diameter $2$, hence the use of transductions. Proving the conjecture would imply that flip-width and merge-width are equivalent, as conjectured by Dreier and Toruńczyk, since bounded flip-width also gives linear neighbourhood complexity and is closed under transductions; the authors also suggest the analogous question for flip-width.
